description: We are team NebulaTech, a group of four enthusiastic engineering students participating in the NASA space Apps Challenge 2026. We are working on developing health monitoring software for astronauts during space missions. Our interests include Python, software development, data analysis, AI and space exploration. We aim to build an innovative and user-friendly solution to help monitor astronaut health and identify unusual health trends.
summary:
ASTRO HEALTH

ASTRO HEALTH is an IoT-based Astronaut Health Monitoring System designed to monitor and support the health of astronauts during space missions. The system uses an ESP32 microcontroller to collect real-time health information through multiple sensors, including the MAX30102 for heart rate and SpO2, DS18B20 for temperature, MPU6050 for movement and activity monitoring, and AD8232 for ECG signal acquisition. The collected data is transmitted wirelessly to a Website and Android application using Bluetooth. The Website and application provide a user-friendly dashboard with live health measurements, interactive human body visualization, health history, charts, and alert notifications. It identifies abnormal readings and provides preventive health recommendations. Additional medical devices can be integrated to monitor blood pressure, blood glucose, and radiation exposure. ASTRO HEALTH aims to improve astronaut health awareness, support early identification of potential health problems, and enable better communication with flight surgeons. This project demonstrates the integration of embedded systems, Website, IoT, mobile applications, and healthcare technology for future space missions.

ASTRO HEALTH

Astronaut Health Monitoring System

1. What does the project do, and how does it work?

ASTRO HEALTH is an IoT-based health monitoring system designed to monitor astronauts' health during space missions. It uses an ESP32 microcontroller connected to multiple sensors to collect health data in real time.

The system uses:

  • MAX30102: Measures heart rate and estimates blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂).
  • DS18B20: Measures skin/contact temperature.
  • MPU6050: Monitors body movement, orientation, and physical activity.
  • AD8232: Captures ECG signals for heart activity monitoring.

The ESP32 sends the collected data wirelessly to an Android application through Wi-Fi or Bluetooth. The application displays readings, graphs, health status, and alerts when measurements require attention.

2. What are the benefits?

  • Enables continuous health monitoring.
  • Helps identify unusual health readings at an early stage.
  • Reduces the need for constant manual monitoring.
  • Provides easy access to health records and trends.
  • Supports communication between astronauts and flight surgeons.
  • Can be expanded with additional medical sensors.

3. What is the intended impact?

The main aim is to improve astronaut health awareness and support safer space missions. The system can help astronauts monitor important health indicators and recognise potential health concerns early. It may also support future remote healthcare systems for people working in isolated or difficult environments.

5. How is the project creative?

ASTRO HEALTH combines embedded systems, IoT, healthcare technology, and mobile application development in one platform. Its creative features include:

  • A futuristic astronaut health dashboard.
  • Real-time sensor monitoring.
  • Interactive human-body health visualisation.
  • Automatic warning notifications.
  • Health history and graphical analysis.
  • Possibility of integrating additional medical devices.

6. What factors did the team consider?

Our team considered:

  1. Accuracy: Using suitable sensors and checking readings before presenting them.
  2. Reliability: Maintaining stable communication between ESP32 and the Android application.
  3. Safety: Avoiding unsupported medical diagnoses and treating alerts as indications for further assessment.
  4. Power efficiency: Designing the system for low-power operation.
  5. User-friendly design: Making the application simple for astronauts to understand and operate.
  6. Space environment: Considering microgravity, radiation, isolation, sleep disruption, and limited access to medical support.
  7. Expandability: Allowing additional sensors and medical devices to be integrated in the future.
